newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hijacker wants release of Pope gunman Agca - police.
newsitem.headline: Hijacker wants release of Pope gunman Agca - police.

text.p: A man who hijacked an Air Malta Boeing 737 airliner to Germany on Monday has demanded the release of Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca, who seriously injured Pope John Paul 11 in an assassination attempt in 1981, German police said.
Police said earlier that the man, who had requested a Turkish-speaking interpreter, had told them he had a bomb on board the plane, which was diverted on a flight from Malta to Istanbul.

"He wants to give a television interview and then give himself up," police spokesman Werner Schmidt told reporters at Cologne-Bonn airport where the plane landed at 4.47 a.m. (0247 GMT) and was standing at a freight section.
Police did not say if they yet knew the identity of the man, who had requested a Turkish-speaking interpreter and a television crew be brought to the airport, 15 km (10 miles) south of Cologne.
Agca shot the Pope in the hand and abdomen as the Pontiff was riding in an open jeep before thousands of people at his general audience in St Peter's Square in Rome. Emergency surgery saved his life.
Agca, whom the Pope later forgave publicly and visited in jail, was wrestled to the ground by pilgrims, including a nun, and is serving a life sentence in Italy.
